We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world.

OfferUp is evolving from a highly transactional local marketplace into a broader platform connecting people with valuable opportunities around them.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager - Member Experience
jobs.description_text:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.

Job Overview:

We are hiring an Engineering Manager to run a squad that builds Omada's Member-facing systems.  A squad owns problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what it ships.  You own that squad: what it works on, in what order, and how the people in it grow.

As an Engineering Manager, you ship code alongside your Builders.  You own the execution and will run the squad’s rituals: iteration shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation - these are your calls.  Owning the call means having a point of view on the tradeoffs behind it, and partnering with your stakeholders to work through the problems that surface along the way.

You partner closely with a Product Strategist who spends their time in front of members, coaches, and stakeholders, and who prototypes to test ideas quickly.  They own what the squad should build and why.  You own whether the squad can deliver it, at what cost, and by when.  You set the quality bar and the operational standard for your squad and will be empowered by both tooling and adaptable processes to hold it.

About you:

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Member Experience
jobs.description_text:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.

Job Overview:

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to own a significant piece of Omada's Member-facing surface. You own what gets built, in what order, and how the people building it grow.

A squad owns problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what it ships. At this level you own more than one, which means the hardest calls you make are the ones about where capacity goes when two good things want it at the same time.

You stay technical. You are in the codebase and in the same agent workflows your builders use, close enough to review architecture, catch a weak design, and be useful in an incident. QuEra Computing is building the world’s most powerful neutral-atom quantum computers. Our systems are designed to scale and enable groundbreaking advances in science and technology. We collaborate closely with leading academic and industry partners to push the boundaries of quantum computing, error correction, and fault tolerance.

QuEra Computing Inc. seeks creative and collaborative Scientific Software Interns to help advance the software that connects high-level quantum applications to neutral-atom quantum computers. Working with software engineers, experimental and computational physicists, and a community of industry and academic collaborators, you will contribute to research and engineering at the intersection of programming languages, compilers, and quantum computing.

We offer a range of research and engineering projects, from investigating new compilation methods and developing prototypes to building software infrastructure and integrating with quantum hardware. Projects span quantum circuits, atom movement, and pulse-level control. Each intern will work with a mentor on a project matched to their interests, experience, and team priorities.

jobs.title: QPU Build Co-Op – Optics & Data Analysis
jobs.description_text:
In this Co-Op/Internship you’ll work at the intersection of optics, atomic physics, and data science. The QPU Build team designs and implements system-wide features of QuEra’s neutral-atom quantum computer architecture. You’ll work hands-on in the lab characterizing the optical systems that trap and control atoms and turn those measurements into insights that drive improvements across the machine. Along the way, you’ll get a holistic view of how a quantum computer is designed and built at QuEra Computing Inc.

Responsibilities

  • Optical Measurements: Design and run measurements to characterize optical components and systems used in neutral-atom quantum computing, including lasers, beam-shaping optics, and atom-trapping setups. Assist with building, aligning, and troubleshooting optical setups in the lab.
  • Data Analysis: Analyze measurement and experimental data using the Python scientific stack. Build tools and workflows that make results reproducible, and turn findings into clear, actionable feedback for the team.
  • System Integration Support: Work with physicists and engineers to bring optical subsystems into the broader atomic physics pipeline and help identify ways to improve performance and reliability.

Qualifications

  • Pursuing or recently completed a degree in physics, optics/photonics, engineering
